This ensures the savings figure (a material fact) resides solely in the strategic initiatives unit (D6) and prevents overlapping evaluation of the same initiative.

redundancy_check.note: All final units were cross-checked for duplicate evaluation targets. After revising D2, no pair substantially overlaps: D1 (headline results) and D2 (Q2 drivers) evaluate distinct aspects; D2 (Q2 expense) and D6 (strategic savings) contain separate material facts; segment, balance sheet, capital, and post-period items remain singular.

key_information_units.information: Q2 2026 headline financial performance showed a decline in profit before tax by 23.7% YoY to ISK 1,545m, driven by resilient net interest income growth of 1.7% YoY to ISK 3,013m offset by a significant 26.8% YoY decrease in net fee and commission income to ISK 1,416m.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Profit before tax ISK 1,545 m. compared to ISK 2,025 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 480 m. or 23.7%; Net interest income ISK 3,013 m. compared to ISK 2,962 m. in Q2 2025 Increasing by ISK 51 m. or 1.7%; Net fee and commission income ISK 1,416 m. compared to ISK 1,935 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 519 m. or 26.8%

key_information_units.information: Major performance drivers in Q2 included the impact of a large ISK 10.2bn dividend payment lowering interest income, a ISK 112m one-off restructuring charge from efficiency measures, and a conservative loan book review resulting in ISK 103m write-downs.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Large dividend: Lowers interest income; Efficiency measures: ISK 112 m. expensed; Conservative loan book review: ISK 103 m. write-downs; Healthy loan book and subdued provisioning needs going forward

key_information_units.information: Strong deposit growth reached ISK 201.2bn (surpassing 200bn for the first time) and loan book expanded to ISK 223.3bn, resulting in a decreased loan-to-deposit ratio to 111% and reflecting continued balance sheet growth.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Deposits amounted to ISK 201.2 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by 16.5% from year-end 2025; Loans to customers amounted to ISK 223.3 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by ISK 15.8 bn., or 7.6%, from year-end 2025; Loan-to-deposit ratio decreased to 111%

key_information_units.information: Segment performances highlighted strong deposit and loan growth in Commercial Banking, resilient lending despite economic challenges in Investment Banking, operational efficiency focus in Asset Management, and sustained deal momentum with record loan book in the UK business.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Commercial Banking: Strong deposit growth, Continued loan book growth; Investment Banking: The loan book grew by nearly 4% quarter-on-quarter; Asset Management: Focus during the quarter remained on improving operational efficiency; UK: The UK business maintained strong activity levels... loan book reaching an all-time high

key_information_units.information: The bank maintained a strong capital and liquidity position with CAR at 23.0%, LCR at 276% (well above requirement), and NSFR at 137%, supported by increased market funding to ISK 101.7bn following senior unsecured and AT1 issuances.
key_information_units.source_evidence: CAR of 23.0% at 30 June 2026; Liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) remains strong at 276%; Net stable funding ratio (NSFR) stood at 137%; Market funding increased to ISK 101.7 bn. at the end of Q2 2026

key_information_units.information: Key strategic initiatives include CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson stepping down by year-end, divestment of Straumur in progress, efficiency measures targeting annual cost savings of ISK 300-400m, and authorization to issue covered bonds in July 2026.
key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson to step down by year-end 2026; Divestment of Straumur expected to close before end of year; Efficiency measures announced in June expected to achieve annualised cost savings of ISK 3-400 m.; In July 2026, Kvika received authorisation to issue covered bonds

key_information_units.information: Material post-reporting-period developments include advancement of the UK stage 3 loan asset sale process expected to close in coming months, and the UK principal investment sale process progressing well with expected closure before year-end.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Sales process for underlying asset of Kvika´s largest stage 3 loan advanced and expected to successfully close in the next months; Q2 saw the receipt of funds following a distribution from a portfolio company, and the sale process for Kvika´s largest principal investment in the UK is progressing well and expected to close before end of year
